messages:
jess_support: Hey — customer `acme-inc` opened a ticket: their app is getting 403s when calling /v1/generate after they upgraded from Starter -> Growth yesterday. They say their API key worked before the upgrade. Error: `403 Forbidden - not_entitled`

deploy-bot: [infra] entitlement-check 1769001234 ran: root_service returned ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED for key-*** masked.

michael_dev: Can you paste the raw response and the curl they used? More specifically, headers + the error body. 403 could be either auth or entitlement.

jess_support: Pasting truncated customer repro: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`
Body: `{"error":"not_entitled","message":"account plan does not allow model redwood-1","code":"ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED"}`
Headers: `x-retry-after: 0`

ashley_billing: We validated the billing account: plan shows Growth, billing active, last invoice paid 2026-03-10. No recent changes to feature gates on our side.

jess_support: Customer says they can still call embeddings and list models, only generation endpoints are 403. They are using the same key for both.

michael_dev: Interesting. Two hypotheses: 1) Entitlement enforcement for generation paths incorrectly mapped to old feature flag name for `redwood-1` so Growth is not matched; 2) The API key scope/enforcement service is splitting by product surface, and the key that routes to generation service is being resolved to the wrong account. Need quick repro from our side with a test key.

clara_sre: I ran an internal repro with a test Growth account key: generation -> 403, embeddings -> 200. Reproduced. Logs from entitlement-resolver show: `requested_feature=gen.redwood-1, resolved_plan=starter, matched=false`.

michael_dev: That log line points to a mapping issue. Can you paste the resolver config? Also, any recent deploys to entitlement-resolver?

deploy-bot: deploy 1768998000 to entitlement-resolver (canary) by @tom_infra — commit: fd3a9b — changed mapping lookup to prefer feature_flag over billing_plan when a `flag_override` exists.

tom_infra: I pushed a small change to support feature flag overrides for A/B testing. In hindsight the fallback order may be inverted for generation features; my change causes flags to override billing plan which is fine for experiments but we missed a default mapping for `gen.redwood-1` => Growth.

ashley_billing: We did create a temporary flag `gen-redwood-primary` that was ON for Starter during a test last week; if the resolver prefers flag overrides, that could explain why it resolved to Starter. I can verify flag state.

jess_support: Customer impact: production traffic 403s since ~10:20 UTC. They rolled back to older app version temporarily. They want ETA to fix.

michael_dev: Quick fix options: 1) revert the canary change to entitlement-resolver (rollback); 2) flip the flag default for `gen-redwood-primary` to off; 3) patch the mapping so flag override respects plan when flag is in a special test pool. I prefer (2) for fastest fix if flag is indeed the culprit.

clara_sre: I can flip the flag globally for the short term. Doing it now...

deploy-bot: flag toggle event: `gen-redwood-primary` set to OFF by clara_sre at 1769002800.

clara_sre: Flag toggle propagated to resolvers in 4s. Re-testing with test Growth key... generation -> 200. Embeddings still 200.

jess_support: Reached out to customer, they confirmed generation now works for their key. :thumbsup:

michael_dev: Root cause: entitlement-resolver change made feature flags take precedence over billing plan. An experimental flag left ON for Starter caused Growth accounts to be treated as Starter for generation surface. So the entitlement check returned ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED. This looked like an auth error to the customer because both surfaces use same API key.

ashley_billing: Action item for Billing/Product: ensure experiments use a dedicated test tenant or a flag targeting only internal orgs. I'll open a follow-up ticket.

tom_infra: Action item for infra/runtime: revert the precedence change or add a more explicit rule: flags should never downgrade a paid plan's entitlements unless targeting internal org ids. I'll prepare a patch.

michael_dev: Also add clearer error code/message for entitlement vs auth: return `401` for invalid key, `403` for entitlement with `code: ENTITLEMENT_REQUIRED` and `meta.plan_expected`. That will help support and customers quickly disambiguate.

jess_support: Drafted the customer reply to close the ticket: 
"Hi — thanks for the report. Root cause was an internal feature flag used for experiments that incorrectly downgraded entitlement for generation endpoints. We've toggled the flag and your requests are now succeeding. Apologies for the disruption; we'll follow up with confirmation when we ship a permanent fix.

If you see any further 403s please send the `x-request-id` header and a curl repro and we'll investigate immediately."

clara_sre: Closing loop: monitor metrics for 2 hours, alert if generation 403 rate > 0.5% for Growth customers. I've set a temporary alert.

michael_dev: I'll pair with tom_infra tomorrow to land the mapping fix + unit tests. Will post PR link.

ashley_billing: I'll create a short doc in product-runbook explaining how to run experiments without touching live entitlement precedence.

jess_support: Thanks everyone — marking ticket resolved for now.

tom_infra: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/entitlement-resolver/pulls/412 — patch reorders precedence and adds whitelist for flag targets. ETA review + canary tomorrow.

michael_dev: Nice. Follow-up: improvement request for support UX: have the SDK return `error.code` in the client exceptions so frontend apps can show friendlier messages (e.g., "Upgrade required: model not in plan"). Logged: https://issues.redwood/internal/SDK-711

jess_support: Great work. :rocket:
